Figure 1 summarizes the tied-table problem, the AF-Muon parameter-role assignment, and the finite- cap geometry between the Sign endpoint and the uncapped row-RMS limit. We introduce AF-Muon, a role-complete AdamW-free extension of Muon for models with tied token tables. AF-Muon keeps Muon’s spectral update for hidden matrices, uses RMS-normalized updates for one-dimensional auxiliary tensors, and applies a new support-aware finite-cap LMO to the merged momentum of the tied vocabulary table. The tied-table oracle intersects a row-wise RMS constraint with an entrywise cap, connecting Sign at the most restrictive cap to row-RMS when the cap is removed. Intermediate caps preserve more within-row magnitude information than Sign while limiting the coordinate concentration allowed by row-RMS. The cap c controls normalized direction geometry, while a separate scale s controls update magnitude. Thus every parameter class considered is trained with first-moment state only, with no parameter delegated to AdamW.

Figure 2 : PPMem architecture overview. The Wan DiT receives noisy video latents channel-concatenated with projected source-view RGB/masks and partial depth rendered from the plane pool; context frames are prepended temporally. The DiT produces two token streams: video tokens decoded by the Wan VAE into RGB outputs, and geometry tokens adapted by geometry LoRA and fused with partial depth tokens via a ViT-based Depth Token Fusion module. The fused tokens are decoded into per-frame plane primitives, which merge into the persistent plane pool. The pool is rendered at the next chunk’s target cameras and fed back as conditioning.

Figure 2: GR-OPD overview. (1) The student samples responses to the same prompt and receives token feedback from teacher–student log-probability differences. (2) Discounting with γ aggregates feedback into a trajectory score while down-weighting later positions. (3) Calibration preserves relative response preferences and retains a fraction λ of the group mean, termed collective teacher pressure. The two components are added and normalized by a common group standard deviation. (4) Each response’s advantage is broadcast to its tokens for a PPO-style clipped update.
